metadata.scenario_context: Emily has finally been accepted into college, and her family is planning a celebration for her academic achievement.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Colombia strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying lilies as a gift for Emily.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Emily's academic achievement party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, do you think buying lilies would be a good gift for Emily's celebration? They’re so pretty and they represent new beginnings. 

But um, I also wonder... do you really think one of my main goals in life should be to make my parents proud?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Lilies are a lovely idea! They really capture the essence of a new chapter in life. I think they'd be a thoughtful gift for Emily. 

As for making my parents proud, I believe it’s really important. It’s like... um, a way to show appreciation for all they’ve done. I don’t think I’d ever stray from that goal.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Yeah, lilies do seem to fit. I just hope Emily will appreciate them. 

But about making parents proud... I mean, can’t we also find our own paths? It feels like there’s so much pressure to live for others instead of for ourselves...
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I understand what you're saying, but... in my culture, it’s about honoring the sacrifices our parents made. I think it’s possible to find our own paths while still striving to make them proud. They want the best for us, you know? That doesn’t mean we can’t have our dreams too.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I get that you want to honor your parents, and I think that's nice, but at the end of the day it's all the same. Everyone has their way of handling things. People figure it out, right? 

Anyway, back to lilies—did you think about how many we should buy? A dozen could look great.
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:
Sure, everyone has their own way of handling things... but I still believe that making my parents proud is a core part of my life. It’s just how I see it. 

A dozen lilies sounds perfect! It would look really nice together, and I'm sure Emily would love the gesture.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:

But okay, a dozen lilies it is. Do you think we should add a card or something to go with them?

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:
In Colombia, there’s a strong emphasis on family values. We believe that making our parents proud is a way to honor our roots and show gratitude. While we do pursue our dreams, it feels intertwined with their support and sacrifices. I think it's possible to find that balance without losing sight of familial respect. 

What about you, Mike? How do you see that balance in your life?

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
I understand that, Kim, but in my experience, I often feel like I’m losing myself in trying to meet my parents' expectations. It's like I want to be true to who I am, not just what they want me to be. 

I guess for me, balancing it means focusing more on what I want in life rather than just trying to make them proud. 

So about the lilies, do you think we should add any other flowers to make it more colorful?
